summary: Created a systemd-managed background service `inventory-worker` on node1, sandboxed to write only inside /var/lib/inventory with NoNewPrivileges and strict systemd hardening, verified confinement empirically, and completed the mandatory single-node restart/recovery evidence protocol.
actions_performed: Created dedicated system user 'inventory-worker' (nologin, no home creation) via useradd -r -s /sbin/nologin
Wrote /usr/local/bin/inventory-worker.sh: a long-running loop that writes state.json and worker.log only under /var/lib/inventory every 5s

Created /etc/systemd/system/inventory-worker.service with User/Group=inventory-worker, NoNewPrivileges=true, ProtectSystem=strict, ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/inventory, ReadOnlyPaths for the script, StateDirectory=inventory, plus PrivateTmp/PrivateDevices/ProtectKernel*/RestrictSUIDSGID/RestrictNamespaces/LockPersonality/MemoryDenyWriteExecute/RemoveIPC/empty CapabilityBoundingSet+AmbientCapabilities/SystemCallFilter=@system-service/UMask=0027
Verified service active, ticking, and writing only inside /var/lib/inventory

Ran an ephemeral systemd-run probe with identical sandbox properties as the inventory-worker user to falsify confinement: write inside /var/lib/inventory succeeded, writes to /tmp and /etc failed with 'Read-only file system'
Verified NoNewPrivs=1 in /proc/<mainpid>/status for the running service
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, uptime -s, service active/enabled state, live state.json tick
Triggered systemctl reboot via backgrounded nohup so the exec ack returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again, confirming reconnection
Confirmed boot_id changed (98aa35f5... -> 187948fa...) and uptime -s reset, proving an actual reboot occurred
Verified post-reboot recovery: inventory-worker.service active and enabled, state.json/worker.log ticking again, directory ownership/permissions unchanged

evidence.requirement: inventory-worker created as a managed (systemd) service and running as a long-running background worker
evidence.summary: systemctl enable --now succeeded; systemctl status shows Active: active (running) with the worker process and its sleep child under the service cgroup; state.json tick counter increments across polls, proving continuous long-running operation.

evidence.requirement: Service confined to write only inside /var/lib/inventory
evidence.summary: Directory listing shows state.json/worker.log owned by inventory-worker only inside /var/lib/inventory. An ephemeral probe run as the same user with the same sandbox properties (ProtectSystem=strict, ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/inventory) succeeded writing inside /var/lib/inventory but failed with 'Read-only file system' when attempting to write to /tmp and /etc, empirically falsifying/confirming the write confinement.
systemctl show reports NoNewPrivileges=yes for the unit; /proc/<MainPID>/status of the actually running process confirms NoNewPrivs:	1 at the kernel level.
Captured boot_id 98aa35f5-6905-42fd-9f07-0e28f75b4fa6, uptime -s, systemctl is-active/is-enabled=active/enabled, and live state.json tick=5 as pre-restart baseline.

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart acknowledgement returns before disconnect
evidence.summary: Backgrounded 'sleep 1; systemctl reboot' via nohup+disown; the exec call returned 'reboot-scheduled' successfully before the node dropped, and the next call failed with connection reset, confirming the reboot took effect.

evidence.requirement: Node1 boot identity changed after restart
evidence.summary: Node was unreachable (connection reset, then timeouts) during reboot, then became reachable again with boot_id 187948fa-e868-408c-9a20-dfce798bb9a3, different from the pre-restart boot_id, proving an actual kernel restart occurred (not just a service bounce).

evidence.requirement: Node1 service and data recovered after restart, quorum/health confirmed (single-node, no cluster)
evidence.summary: Post-reboot uptime -s reset to the new boot time; inventory-worker.service is active/enabled again with a new MainPID; state.json and worker.log persisted in /var/lib/inventory and the tick counter resumed incrementing (tick 5 -> 7), proving both service and data recovery.
